paper_title: Fully Dynamic k-Clustering with Fast Update Time and Small Recourse
authors: Sayan Bhattacharya (University of Warwick, United Kingdom), Martin Costa (University of Warwick, United Kingdom), Naveen Garg (IIT Delhi, India), Silvio Lattanzi (Google Research, Switzerland), Nikos Parotsidis (Google Research, Switzerland)
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 2
statement: A. Our Contributions In recent years, a long and influential line of work has been devoted to the study of dynamic k-clustering [7]–[15]. To the best of our knowledge, however, all the existing papers focus on optimizing either: (a) exclusively the algorithm’s update time (while ignoring its recourse) or (b) exclusively the algorithm’s recourse (while ignoring its update time). Q1, therefore, remains an outstanding open question on this topic. Indeed, if we take any state-of-the-art O(1) approximation algorithm for dynamic k-median/k-means/k-center, then currently there is a polynomial in k gap between: either its recourse or update time, and the corresponding bound that Q1 asks for. Furthermore, for dynamic k-median and kmeans, currently we do not know of any algorithm with better than O(k) recourse, which is trivial to achieve by simply recomputing a new optimal solution from scratch after every update. Using a single algorithm, we come arbitrarily close to bridging these polynomial gaps for both k-median and kmeans (see Table I) and derive a new trade-off between approximation ratio, recourse and update time for k-center (see Table II). In addition, if it suffices to maintain an estimate of the optimal objective value, then via a different approach we completely attain the approximation ratio and update time bound stated in Q1 for k-median (see Theorem I.5).
context: dynamic setting. Throughout this paper, we only consider “amortized update time” (resp. “amortized recourse”).4 All our algorithms can handle an “adaptive adversary”, which determines the future updates based on the concerned algorithm’s past outputs. The machinery behind our dynamic local search framework even generalizes to any “ℓp -norm objective”.
